mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown; this combination predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of RSAFS and HOUST declining together fails to predict negative 60-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing contraction (INDPRO below 95), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate investment and earnings growth; this regime predicts negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95 (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 new jobs per month indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS > 100,000 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of persistently high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) and a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates a prolonged monetary easing cycle in response to weak labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5% AND FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate above 2.5%), the S&P 500 tends to outperform due to robust corporate earnings; this regime predicts positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).
